🎯 EXAM ORAL DEFENSE PROTOCOL

How to Answer Any Examiner Question

Answer in this order: What it does → Why we chose it → Proof → Boundary.

Search the story ID or topic. Say the blue “Say This First” sentence. Open lineage only when asked for proof. If incomplete, say the limitation—never improvise.

🗣️ 5-Sentence Rehearsable Answer Pattern

“This feature lets [role] do [business outcome].

We chose it because [requirement/risk].

The key trade-off was [alternative rejected].

We prove it with [PR/run/code path].

Its current boundary is [honest limitation].”

Example (Venue Block precision): Do not say it “prevents blocks over confirmed bookings.” State precisely: “A venue block can be created over confirmed bookings without being blocked: the block saves, overlapping bookings become Conflicting, and the confirmed event returns to Planning for resolution.”
Legend: ✅ Done Code, tests, and evidence linked ⚠️ Partial Implemented but evidence/gate incomplete 🚨 Open defect Not counted as Done 📌 Historical decision Context, not proof of delivery

TOPIC 02 Concurrency Enforced (T-66) SCRUM-44 / SCRUM-50

Venue Setup & Turnaround Buffers

C-18/C-38 excluded → C-65/T-66 reinstated → T-100 claim reservation → 0016_venue_buffer_write_guard.sql
SAY THIS FIRST (ELEVATOR DEFENSE)

"Buffers are per-venue whole minutes applied before start and after end; PostgreSQL exclusion constraints guard the buffered range against overlapping bookings, holds, and concurrent booking race conditions, while buffer edits flag existing bookings as Conflicting rather than silently dropping them."

Code Reality: Occupancy window is [starts_at - setup_minutes, ends_at + turnaround_minutes]. Maintenance blocks are venue properties and are NOT buffered (T-80). Guards booking race conditions.

Primary Code: backend/src/modules/venueBooking/decisions.ts
Real DB Test: backend/tests/venueBufferConflicts.integration.test.ts

TOPIC 03 Specification Delta Shipped T-92 SCRUM-49

Tentative Holds: Shipped T-92 vs Target T-84

C-01/C-16 deprioritised → C-68/T-69 expiry mandatory → T-92 shipped default vs T-84 student target
SAY THIS FIRST (ELEVATOR DEFENSE)

"In production code, holds follow team decision T-92 with a 48-hour default and instant SQL expiry on clock_timestamp(); the student backlog spec was updated to T-84 (per-hold custom expiry, max 2 reasoned extensions), leaving T-84 as an accepted backlog delta."

Code Reality: A hold ceases occupying a venue immediately when expires_at <= clock_timestamp(), even before the cron cleanup runs. Converted holds that become formal pending requests never restore hold expiry upon withdrawal.

TOPIC 05 Concurrency Bug Fix Fixed in PR #239 SCRUM-57

Technician Deadlock & Lock Order (PR #239)

E07-S07 flaky CI on exclusion constraint → PR #239 root cause diagnosis → FOR NO KEY UPDATE fix
SAY THIS FIRST (ELEVATOR DEFENSE)

"Concurrent technician assignments deadlocked on PostgreSQL exclusion constraints (40P01); PR #239 resolved this booking race by enforcing an explicit lock order: locking the request FOR UPDATE, then locking the technician's user row FOR NO KEY UPDATE before checking clashes."

Code Reality: FOR NO KEY UPDATE prevents blocking foreign-key references (e.g. notifications). Handled 40P01 backstop as a 409 clash. Verified by a 25-round concurrent race test in CI.

Primary Code: backend/src/modules/equipmentSupport/staffAssignments.ts:88
Real DB Test: backend/tests/staffAssignments.integration.test.ts
DB Migration: backend/database/migrations/0001_connectsphere_schema.sql
Key Test Cases: TC_E07S07_03
TOPIC 06 Race Protection Shipped (T-85/T-98) SCRUM-64 / SCRUM-66

Attendee Capacity & Waitlist Races

C-78/C-97/C-107 → T-85 dual capacity limits → T-98 event-level waitlist
SAY THIS FIRST (ELEVATOR DEFENSE)

"Dual attendee capacity guards enforce per-session and event-level caps in SQL; registration locks the parent event row to prevent oversubscription across concurrent signups, and if an individual session is full, the registration routes to Pending for Organiser review."

Code Reality: Waitlist is strictly event-level (T-98). Freed places trigger a simultaneous broadcast notification to all waitlisted attendees for a first-come claim race (C-23, T-46); no automated FIFO seat bumping.

Real DB Test: backend/tests/attendeeRegistration.integration.test.ts

Transactional Outbox & Brevo Rollback

C-04/T-35 delivery channel → ADR-006 transactional outbox → 0002_durable_notification_dispatch.sql
SAY THIS FIRST (ELEVATOR DEFENSE)

"External email delivery via Brevo never runs inline with business logic; notification records are persisted to an atomic PostgreSQL outbox table inside the business transaction, ensuring zero orphaned emails if a transaction rolls back."

Code Reality: Worker polls pending rows with exponential backoff up to 5 retries. Tests intercept HTTP requests at provider boundary to guarantee 100% offline isolation.

Log in to the system

SAY THIS FIRST (10-SEC HOOK)

"Login verifies bcrypt credentials, creates an HTTP-only secure session cookie, and triggers automatic account lockout after 5 consecutive failed attempts."

Known Limitation / Boundary: Lockout is account-specific, reset via email token with 15-minute expiration; failed login returns generic credentials error without disclosing email existence.
BDR References: C-30, T-38, O-02

Expand Full Lineage & Technical Proof

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Valid credentials accepted

Given I am a registered user with valid credentials When I submit my email address and password Then I am signed in and taken to the dashboard for my role

Scenario 2 — Wrong password reveals nothing

Given I am a registered user When I submit an incorrect password Then I remain signed out and see a message that does not reveal whether the email address is registered

Scenario 3 — Lockout on fifth failure

Given I have submitted 5 consecutive incorrect passwords When I attempt to sign in again Then my account is locked and I am shown how to reset my password

Scenario 4 — Reset link issued

Given my account is locked When I request a password reset Then a reset link is sent to my registered email address

Scenario 5 — Lock lifted on new password

Given I have followed a valid reset link When I set a new password Then the lock is lifted and I can sign in with the new password

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (6 criteria)

  • ☑ Sign in with a valid email and password and reach the dashboard for my role
  • ☑ Be refused on an incorrect password without learning whether the email is registered
  • ☑ Be locked out on the 5th consecutive failed attempt
  • ☑ Receive a reset link at my registered email address
  • ☑ Regain access once the password has been reset
  • ☑ Have the lockout recorded in the activity log (E14-S02)

Technical Slice Architecture

Route / Endpoint: POST /api/auth/session, POST /api/auth/recover
Backend Controller: backend/src/modules/accessControl/sessions.ts
Database Migration: 0003_auth_sessions.sql, 0007_password_reset_delivery.sql
Frontend Component: frontend/src/features/accessControl/LoginPage.tsx

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Own client's events only

Given I am signed in as an Event Organiser for Client A When I open my event list Then only events belonging to Client A are shown

Scenario 2 — Direct access refused

Given an event belongs to a client organisation I am not linked to When I navigate directly to that event's identifier Then access is refused and the attempt is recorded in the activity log

Scenario 3 — Colleague's event visible

Given my organisation has several Event Organisers When a colleague from my organisation creates an event Then I can see that event in my organisation's list

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (6 criteria)

  • ☑ View only events linked to their own client organisation in their event list
  • ☑ Be denied access when attempting to open (e.g. via URL or ID) an event belonging to another client organisation
  • ☑ View events created by any Organiser within their own client organisation
  • ☑ Search for events without unrelated client organisations' events appearing in the results
  • ☑ Receive notifications that never reference events belonging to unrelated client organisations
  • ☑ Confirm that a denied access attempt is captured in the activity log with the user, event and time

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Published details only

Given I am signed in as an Attendee and registered for an event When I view that event Then I see the published name, date, time and venue, and no Coordinator notes, booking decisions, equipment reservations or internal comments

Scenario 2 — Internal screen refused

Given I am signed in as an Attendee When I attempt to open an internal planning screen Then access is refused and the attempt is recorded in the activity log

TC_E01S11_01 TC_E01S11_02 TC_E01S11_03 TC_E01S11_04 TC_E01S11_05
Expand Full Lineage & Technical Proof

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Deactivated and signed out

Given I am signed in When I confirm deactivation Then I am signed out and can no longer sign in with those credentials

Scenario 2 — Historical records retained

Given I have deactivated my account When ConnectSphere views an event I was linked to Then my past registrations and event records remain intact and attributed

Scenario 3 — Upcoming registration released

Given I am an Attendee registered for an upcoming event (an event whose start timestamp is in the future) When I deactivate Then my registration is withdrawn and the place is released, and this applies to both `registered` and `waitlisted` entries, and deactivation overrides the E09-S05 `withdrawal_deadline` (see T-53, T-54, T-55)

Scenario 4 — Coordinator with events blocked

Given I am an Event Coordinator with events assigned to me in an active-lifecycle status (Submitted, Under review, Clarification requested, Approved, Planning, or Confirmed) When I attempt to deactivate Then deactivation is blocked until those events are reassigned, while events in Completed, Cancelled, or Rejected status do not block deactivation (see T-52)

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (6 criteria)

  • ☑ Deactivate my own account and be signed out immediately
  • ☑ Be unable to sign in afterwards
  • ☑ Have my historical event and registration records retained and still attributed
  • ☑ Have upcoming registrations (event start in the future) released on deactivation, including waitlisted entries, overriding the E09-S05 withdrawal deadline (Attendees; T-53, T-54, T-55)
  • ☑ Be blocked from deactivating while I hold any event in an active-lifecycle status (Submitted through Confirmed); events in Completed, Cancelled, or Rejected do not block (Coordinators; T-52)
  • ☑ Have the deactivation recorded in the activity log with actor and time

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Previous event copied

Given I choose one of my own completed or past events When I copy it Then ConnectSphere creates a new draft with the event requirements and Session structure copied, all event and Session dates/times left blank, and no bookings, reservations, or registrations carried over (T-99)

Scenario 2 — Missing reference flagged

Given the copied event references a venue or equipment item that no longer exists When the draft is created Then the affected requirement is flagged for review and identifies its Session rather than being copied silently

Scenario 3 — Dates remain subject to current submission policy

Given I later submit the copied draft When I enter event and Session dates Then the current E02-S01 and E02-S07 validation applies; copying does not bypass the two-year horizon or the Coordinator feasibility review

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (5 criteria)

  • ☑ Copy one of my own completed or past events into a new draft
  • ☑ Confirm requirements and Session structure are copied while event and Session dates/times are blank
  • ☑ Confirm bookings, equipment reservations and registrations are not copied (T-99)
  • ☑ See unavailable venue/equipment references flagged against the relevant Session
  • ☑ Submit a copied draft subject to the current date rules

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — No fixed minimum lead time

Given a requested event date is not in the past and is within the permitted horizon When I submit the request Then ConnectSphere does not reject it solely because it is fewer than a fixed number of days or months away; the assigned Coordinator assesses feasibility

Scenario 2 — Dates beyond two years rejected

Given any requested event or Session date is later than two calendar years after the Singapore-local submission date When I submit the request Then submission is blocked and the out-of-range date is identified

Scenario 3 — Two-year boundary accepted

Given every requested event and Session date is on or before the date two calendar years after the Singapore-local submission date When I submit an otherwise valid request Then the date-horizon check passes

Scenario 4 — Past Event date rule preserved

Given the requested Event date is in the past When I submit the request Then E02-S01 past-date validation still blocks it

Scenario 5 — Past Session date rejected

Given any requested Session date is in the past When I submit the request Then submission is blocked and the past Session date is identified

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (5 criteria)

  • ☑ Submit a feasible request without an invented minimum lead time
  • ☑ Be blocked when any Event or Session date exceeds two calendar years from submission
  • ☑ Pass the exact two-year boundary
  • ☑ Confirm a past Event date remains blocked by E02-S01
  • ☑ Be blocked when any Session date is in the past

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — [Superseded by E03-S08 (C-69)] Exactly one Coordinator assigned

Given a request is submitted When submission completes Then the system assigns exactly one Event Coordinator, the status becomes Under Review, and that Coordinator is notified

Scenario 2 — [Superseded by E03-S08 (C-69)] Fewest active events wins

Given several Event Coordinators are available When the system assigns one Then it selects the Coordinator with the fewest active events

Scenario 3 — Reassignment requested

Given I am the assigned Coordinator and a reassignment has been agreed offline When I request reassignment to a named colleague Then the request is recorded, that colleague is notified, and I remain assigned until they accept

Scenario 4 — Reassignment accepted

Given a reassignment request is awaiting my acceptance When I accept it Then I become the assigned Coordinator, the previous assignment ends, and the change is recorded in the activity log

Scenario 5 — Reassignment declined

Given a reassignment request is awaiting acceptance When the named colleague declines it Then the original Coordinator remains assigned and is notified of the refusal

Scenario 6 — Unassigned Coordinator refused

Given I am not the assigned Coordinator When I attempt to reassign the event Then the action is refused

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (8 criteria)

  • ☑ Confirm that exactly one Event Coordinator is assigned on submission (superseded by E03-S08, C-69)
  • ☑ Confirm the assigned Coordinator is the one with the fewest active events (superseded by E03-S08, C-69; the count is now shown to the Lead as advice)
  • ☑ Confirm the status moves from Submitted to Under Review
  • ☑ Request reassignment to a named colleague as the assigned Coordinator
  • ☑ Confirm the original Coordinator stays assigned until the colleague accepts
  • ☑ Accept a reassignment request and take ownership of the event
  • ☑ Decline a reassignment request, leaving the original Coordinator assigned
  • ☑ Be refused when attempting to reassign an event assigned to someone else

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Approved to planning

Given a request has status Under Review and the required information is complete When I approve it Then the status becomes Approved and the Event Organiser is notified

Given required information is still incomplete When I try to approve the request Then approval is blocked and the missing items are listed

Scenario 3 — Rejected with reason

Given a request is under review When I reject it and record a reason Then the status becomes Rejected, the reason is stored and the Event Organiser is notified

Scenario 4 — Rejection without reason blocked

Given I attempt to reject without recording a reason When I confirm Then the rejection is blocked

Scenario 5 — Rejected record is read-only

Given a request has been rejected When the Event Organiser views it Then the reason and the date of the decision are shown and the request is read-only

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (8 criteria)

  • ☑ Approve a request whose required information is complete
  • ☑ Confirm an approval sets the status to Approved and notifies the Organiser
  • ☑ Be blocked from approving an incomplete request, with the missing items listed
  • ☑ Reject a request under review with a recorded reason
  • ☑ Be blocked from rejecting without a recorded reason
  • ☑ Confirm a rejection sets the status to Rejected and notifies the Organiser
  • ☑ See the reason and decision date in plain language as the Organiser
  • ☑ Confirm a rejected request is read-only

Given I do not have access to an event When I attempt to post a comment Then the action is refused

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (5 criteria)

  • ☑ Be refused when posting on an event I cannot access

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Submission enters the unassigned queue

Given an Event Organiser submits a request When submission completes Then no Event Coordinator is assigned, the event's status stays Submitted, the request appears in the unassigned queue, and every active Event Coordinator Lead is notified (replaces E03-S01 Scenarios 1 and 2)

Scenario 2 — Queue shows basic event information, oldest first

Given requests are in the unassigned queue When I open it as an Event Coordinator Lead Then each shows the event name, the Organiser's client organisation, preferred dates, expected attendance and the time submitted, oldest first; every Lead sees the same organisation-wide queue, and no non-Lead can view it

Scenario 3 — Lead assigns a Coordinator

Given a request is in the queue When I, as an Event Coordinator Lead, choose an Event Coordinator and assign them Then exactly one Coordinator is assigned immediately, the status becomes Under Review, the Coordinator and the Organiser are notified, the request leaves the queue, and the activity log records the Lead actor and time

Scenario 4 — Workload shown while choosing

Given I am choosing a Coordinator When the list of Coordinators is shown Then each shows their count of active events, so the fewest-active-events rule the system used to apply (T-14) is available as advice without being enforced

Scenario 5 — Only a Lead may assign from the queue

Given I am not an Event Coordinator Lead When I attempt to view or assign a queued request Then the action is refused and the refusal is recorded in the activity log

Scenario 6 — Status transition and Organiser view unchanged

Given a request has been assigned from the queue When the Organiser tracks the event (E03-S05) Then the status history shows Submitted followed by Under Review exactly as it did under automatic assignment, so E03-S01's delivered transition still holds

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (7 criteria)

  • ☑ Confirm a newly submitted request has no Coordinator, stays Submitted and appears in the unassigned queue
  • ☑ Confirm every active Lead is notified of each new queued request
  • ☑ See the same global queued requests and basic information, oldest first, as any Lead only
  • ☑ Assign exactly one Coordinator from the queue, moving the event to Under Review with the Coordinator and Organiser notified and the action logged
  • ☑ See each Coordinator's active-event count while choosing
  • ☑ Be refused as a non-Lead when attempting to view or assign from the queue
  • ☑ Confirm the Submitted to Under Review transition recorded by E03-S01 is unchanged

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Shared success Alert after a saved edit

Given I may edit an event When a changed field saves successfully Then the event detail shows the existing field-specific saved message through the shared Alert with tone="success", retaining role="status" rather than replacing it with an urgent alert or plain paragraph.

Scenario 2 — Saved data and audit survive reload

Given an allowed event edit succeeds When the record reloads and I reopen it Then the changed value is retained and its existing activity-log entry remains available, with no extra save or audit write caused by rendering the confirmation.

Scenario 3 — Failure cannot report success

Given a new edit is invalid or its save request fails When I attempt to save Then the existing validation or error feedback remains and no success Alert claims that attempt was saved; starting a new edit clears the previous save confirmation.

Scenario 4 — Cancellation and permissions unchanged

Given I cancel an edit or attempt a field I cannot edit under the current event status and access rules When the attempt ends Then cancellation produces no save confirmation or mutation, and existing restrictions and change-request routing remain in force.

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Sessions hold their own requirements

Given I am creating an event When I add one or more Sessions Then each Session stores its date, time, expected attendance, venue requirements, and equipment requirements beneath the Event

Scenario 2 — Single-session event needs no extra setup

Given my event has one Session When I create it Then the system supports it as a single-session Event without requiring extra registration or lifecycle setup

Scenario 3 — Suitability judged per Session

Given two Sessions have different attendance or requirements When venue suitability is assessed for each Then each assessment uses that Session's own requirements and attendance

Scenario 4 — Session booking is independent

Given one Event uses the same venue for different Sessions When bookings are requested Then each booking is linked to its Session and its own time window; a booking for one Session does not replace another Session's booking

Scenario 5 — Deleted Session releases its booking

Given a Session has a confirmed venue booking When I delete that Session Then the booking is released, Venue Staff are notified, and the deletion is recorded in the activity log

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (5 criteria)

  • ☑ Add one or more Sessions beneath an Event with their own date, time, attendance, venue and equipment requirements
  • ☑ Create a single-session Event without extra lifecycle steps
  • ☑ Assess venue suitability against each Session independently
  • ☑ Link bookings to the Session whose period they cover
  • ☑ Delete a Session and release its confirmed booking with notification and history

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Venue added and searchable

Given I am adding a venue When I save it with location, capacity, facilities, accessibility features, supported layouts and operating hours Then it becomes searchable by Event Coordinators

Scenario 2 — Capacity drop flags bookings

Given a venue has confirmed bookings When I reduce its capacity below the expected attendance of one of those bookings Then the affected bookings are flagged for review and the assigned Coordinators are notified

Scenario 3 — Venue retired

Given a venue has no future bookings When I retire it Then it no longer appears in search results and its past bookings are retained

Scenario 4 — Retirement blocked by future bookings

Given a venue has future bookings When I attempt to retire it Then retirement is blocked and the blocking bookings are identified

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (6 criteria)

  • ☑ Add a venue with location, capacity, facilities, accessibility features, supported layouts and operating hours
  • ☑ Update any of those attributes on an existing venue
  • ☑ Confirm a new venue becomes searchable by Event Coordinators
  • ☑ Confirm affected bookings are flagged when capacity drops below a booked attendance
  • ☑ Retire a venue that has no future bookings
  • ☑ Be blocked from retiring a venue with future bookings, with those bookings identified

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Four states distinguishable

Given a venue has bookings and blocks in a period When I open its calendar for that period Then each entry is shown as Free, Tentative, Confirmed or Blocked, and the states are visually distinguishable

Given I do not have permission to view another event's details When I open the calendar Then the period is shown as unavailable without revealing the other event's information

Scenario 3 — Block distinct from booking

Given a venue is blocked for maintenance When I view the calendar Then the block is clearly distinct from a booking

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (6 criteria)

  • ☑ See the availability state for each period: Free, Tentative, Confirmed or Blocked
  • ☑ See the event name, event, date and time for periods I am permitted to view
  • ☑ Navigate to different dates or date ranges
  • ☑ See a blocked venue clearly distinguished from a booked one
  • ☑ See periods I cannot view marked unavailable without any event detail

🔗 Jira Ticket (SCRUM-44) 🔀 Pull Request #234 💻 Source (catalogue.ts) 🧪 Test (venueBufferConflicts.integration.test.ts) 📋 Run Evidence (20261106-081527-Bl0oper-backend-db.md) Coverage: 8 active / 8 total

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Buffers recorded on the venue

Given I am creating or editing a venue When I enter a setup time and a turnaround time in whole minutes, either of which may be 0, and save Then both values are stored against the venue and shown on its detail, and every venue that existed before this story has both values at 0

Scenario 2 — Occupancy window computed from the buffers

Given a venue has a setup time of 30 minutes and a turnaround time of 45 minutes When a booking or tentative hold for 10:00 to 12:00 is evaluated for availability or conflicts Then the venue is treated as occupied from 09:30 to 12:45

Scenario 3 — Calendar shows the buffered window

Given a venue with non-zero buffers has a Confirmed booking or a Tentative hold When a Coordinator or Venue Staff member views the venue availability calendar Then the Confirmed or Tentative period shown covers the buffered window and the buffer portion is visually distinguishable from the advertised event time, and the Free, Tentative, Confirmed and Blocked states of E05-S03 are otherwise unchanged

Scenario 4 — Conflicts created by a buffer change are identified, not removed

Given a venue has Confirmed bookings 10:00 to 12:00 and 12:30 to 14:00 and a turnaround time of 0 When I change the turnaround time to 45 minutes and save Then the save succeeds (assumes O-21), both bookings remain Confirmed and the later one is marked Conflicting rather than released, the conflicting pair is listed to me on save, the calendar flags the conflict, and the Coordinator of each affected event is notified (assumes O-20)

Scenario 5 — Buffers do not apply against a maintenance block

Given a venue has a maintenance block ending at 12:00 and a setup time of 30 minutes When a booking request for 12:00 to 14:00 is evaluated Then the block and the booking are compared on the booking's advertised times, so the request is not in conflict with the block (assumes O-22)

Scenario 6 — Adjacent buffered windows do not conflict

Given booking A occupies a venue until 12:45 once its turnaround is applied When booking B's buffered window on the same venue starts at exactly 12:45 Then there is no conflict, and when it starts at 12:44 there is

Scenario 7 — Buffered occupancy excludes a venue from search

Given a venue's existing booking or hold, once that venue's setup and turnaround time are applied, overlaps an event's requested period When a Coordinator runs the venue search for that event Then the venue does not appear as available even though the advertised event times do not overlap; E06-S01 is Done and is not edited, this is its buffered-search requirement placed here under T-74

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (5 criteria)

  • ☑ Record a setup time and a turnaround time in whole minutes for each venue, with 0 allowed and 0 the default for existing venues
  • ☑ See both values on the venue's detail
  • ☑ Have the calendar, venue search, booking request, booking decision, tentative hold and double-booking prevention all evaluate the buffered occupancy window instead of the advertised event times
  • ☑ See the conflicts a buffer change creates listed on save and flagged on the calendar, with the affected Coordinators notified
  • ☑ Never have a booking released automatically because a buffer changed

Technical Slice Architecture

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Unavailability recorded with a reason

Given I am viewing a venue When I mark it unavailable from a start date and time, with an optional end date and time, and choose a reason category from maintenance, equipment failure, renovation, safety concern or other, with a free-text note Then the unavailability is saved with the period, the category, the note and my identity, and the calendar shows the period as Blocked; with no end, it shows as Blocked from its start until it is lifted (T-80)

Scenario 2 — Overlapping bookings become Conflicting, not released

Given the venue has a Pending request and a Confirmed booking inside the period When I save the unavailability Then the save succeeds, both bookings are marked Conflicting, neither is released or cancelled, and the two affected events are listed to me on save; overlap is judged on each booking's advertised times, not its setup and turnaround buffers (T-80); an unexpired Tentative hold inside the period is flagged Conflicting in the same way, is not released, and its event is listed and its Coordinator notified as in Scenario 4 (C-111)

Scenario 3 — A Confirmed event returns to Planning, not cancelled

Given a Confirmed event's active venue booking has just become Conflicting When the unavailability is saved Then the event returns to Planning automatically and is not cancelled, every other arrangement is intact, and a venue-conflict flag with the reason category is shown on the event; an affected event that was not Confirmed keeps its status (C-120, T-81)

Scenario 4 — Affected Coordinators informed

Given the unavailability made one or more bookings Conflicting When it is saved Then the Coordinator of each affected event immediately receives an in-app and email notification naming the venue, the period, the reason category and the event, and stating that alternative arrangements are required; the Organiser and registered Attendees are not notified at this point (C-121, T-81)

Scenario 5 — Open-ended or extended unavailability

Given I am recording an unavailability When I leave the end date and time empty Then it is saved as open-ended and stays in force until it is lifted; and Given a saved unavailability When I extend its end or remove its end Then bookings newly inside the longer period are handled as in Scenarios 2 to 4 (T-80, T-91)

Scenario 6 — Unavailability shortened, lifted or ended early

Given a booking is Conflicting only because of an unavailability When I shorten or lift that unavailability so the booking no longer overlaps it Then the Conflicting flag clears and the booking returns to the status it had before, Pending, Confirmed or Tentative, except that a hold whose expiry has passed in the meantime becomes Expired (E06-S05); a booking the Coordinator has already cancelled or replaced is not restored; an event already returned to Planning follows E08-S04 Scenario 4 rather than returning straight to Confirmed (C-122, T-81)

Scenario 7 — Edits and lifts keep their history

Given an unavailability exists When I edit its period or reason, or lift it Then a history entry keeps the earlier and new period and reason with my identity and the time, a lifted unavailability is kept rather than deleted, and when it is lifted the Coordinator of each event whose booking it made Conflicting is notified (T-91)

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (8 criteria)

  • ☑ Mark a venue unavailable from a start date and time, with an optional end, a reason category and a note, including when Pending or Confirmed bookings fall inside the period
  • ☑ See the affected events listed on save and their bookings and unexpired holds marked Conflicting, with none released or cancelled
  • ☑ Confirm an affected Confirmed event returns to Planning without being cancelled, keeps its other arrangements and shows a venue-conflict flag
  • ☑ Confirm each affected Coordinator is notified in-app and by email, and the Organiser and registered Attendees are not
  • ☑ Save an open-ended unavailability, and extend an existing one so bookings newly inside it are flagged
  • ☑ Confirm shortening or lifting an unavailability clears the Conflicting flag on bookings it no longer touches and restores their earlier status
  • ☑ Confirm each edit and lift keeps a history entry, and a lift notifies the affected Coordinators
  • ☑ Confirm E05-S04's existing block, shorten and remove behaviour still works for periods with no bookings

Scenario 1 — Matching venues listed

Scenario 2 — Near matches show failing criteria

Given no venue matches all criteria When I run the search Then near matches are returned rather than an empty result

Scenario 3 — Undersized venue marked unsuitable

Given a venue is available but its capacity is below the event's expected attendance When results are displayed Then it is excluded or clearly marked as unsuitable

Scenario 4 — Blocked or booked venues excluded

Given a venue is blocked or already confirmed the event's period When I run the search Then it does not appear as available

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (6 criteria)

  • ☑ See near matches returned rather than an empty result when nothing matches fully
  • ☑ Confirm venues below the event's attendance are excluded or marked unsuitable
  • ☑ Confirm blocked or already-confirmed venues do not appear as available
  • ☑ Apply several filters together in one search

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Suitability shown for the event

Given an event has recorded requirements When I view a venue in the context of the event Then a suitability status is shown for the event

Scenario 2 — Failing requirements named

Given a venue fails one or more recorded requirements When I view it Then it is marked unsuitable and every failing requirement is named

Scenario 3 — All requirements met

Given a venue meets all recorded requirements for the event When I view it Then it is marked suitable

Scenario 4 — Unsuitable venue may still be requested

Given a venue is marked unsuitable When I submit a booking request for it anyway Then the request is accepted and the unsuitability is shown to the Venue Staff for their decision

Scenario 5 - Operating hours checked without blocking booking (T-77)

Given an event has recorded start and end times When I check a venue's suitability Then an event outside the venue's operating hours is marked Unsuitable with "outside operating hours" explicitly named; an event fully within the hours passes this criterion. Suitability remains advisory and an unsuitable venue may still be requested, with its failures shown to Venue Staff for their decision. Product Owner clarification relayed on 8 October 2026. E06-S01 operating hours remain display-only; its search behaviour is unchanged. Use the existing Singapore timezone and daily opening-window convention. Exact opening and closing times are within hours. This is event-based; T-21's sessions wording is withdrawn by T-48.

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Request created as Pending

Given an event has recorded requirements and no pending request When I submit a booking request for a venue Then the request is created with status Pending, the venue calendar shows the period as Tentative, and the Venue Staff are notified

Scenario 2 — First request moves event to Planning

Given the event has status Approved When its first booking request is submitted Then the event status becomes Planning

Scenario 3 — Several venue bookings for one event

Given the event already has a Pending or Confirmed venue booking When I submit a request for another venue, or for the same venue over a different period, for the same event Then the request is created as Pending alongside the existing bookings, each booking keeps its own status, the event lists all of them, and withdrawing or changing one booking leaves the others untouched (C-67, T-68; replaces the earlier rule that blocked a second request, T-20 retired)

Scenario 4 — Venue taken by another event blocked

Given a venue is already Pending or Confirmed for another event over the same period When I submit a request for it Then submission is blocked and the conflict is explained

Scenario 5 — Request conflicts through the buffer

Given a venue is Confirmed for another event 10:00 to 12:00 and has a turnaround time of 45 minutes When I submit a request for 12:30 to 14:00 Then submission is blocked and the conflict names the other event's buffered window, 09:30 to 12:45 (C-65, T-66) Confirmed-primary cancellation is a future separate flow: clear primary and prompt the Organiser to select another Confirmed venue, with no automatic promotion (T-94). This does not implement that flow or change the existing Coordinator selection permission in Scenario 3c.

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (11 criteria)

  • ☑ Submit a booking request only as the assigned Event Coordinator while the event is Approved or Planning, using its recorded requirements (T-78)
  • ☑ Confirm the request is created as Pending and Venue Staff are notified
  • ☑ Confirm the venue calendar shows the period as Tentative
  • ☑ Confirm the event status moves from Approved to Planning on the first request
  • ☑ Hold several venue bookings, Pending or Confirmed, for one event, each with an optional purpose and headcount, and mark one as primary (C-67; confirmed O-27 and O-30, T-78)
  • ☑ Be blocked from requesting a venue already Pending or Confirmed for another event in that period, counting that venue's setup and turnaround time (C-65)
  • ☑ View the status of each of my booking requests
  • ☑ Withdraw only a Pending request to Released, preserving other bookings and the event status; notify the requested venue's assigned staff (T-94, T-95)
  • ☑ Serialize withdrawal against approval/rejection and retain the booking-specific audit history (T-95)
  • ☑ Allow a new replacement after withdrawal; after rejection follow only the latest rejection's own suggestion (T-96)
  • ☑ Complete TC_E06S03_09 to _13 under the current Sprint 3 plan; record anything unfinished honestly at sprint close (PO confirmation, 16 October; T-94)

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Request approved and confirmed

Given a booking request is pending and the venue is free for the period When I approve it Then the booking becomes Confirmed, the venue calendar is updated and the Coordinator is notified

Scenario 2 — Rejected with reason and alternative

Given I reject a request When I record a reason and optionally suggest an alternative venue Then the Coordinator is notified with both, and can amend the request to the suggested alternative without restarting the search

Scenario 3 — Rejection without reason blocked

Given I attempt to reject without recording a reason When I confirm Then the rejection is blocked

Scenario 4 — Approval checks the buffered window

Given approving a pending request would make its buffered occupancy window overlap another Confirmed booking's buffered window on the same venue When I approve it Then approval is blocked and the conflicting booking is identified, even if the two advertised event times do not overlap (C-65, T-66)

Scenario 5 — Booking decision recorded

Given a venue booking is approved, rejected or released When the action completes Then an entry is recorded with the actor, the action, the affected records and the time

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (9 criteria)

  • ☑ Approve a pending booking request for a free venue
  • ☑ Confirm the booking becomes Confirmed and the calendar updates
  • ☑ Reject a request with a recorded reason
  • ☑ Be blocked from rejecting without a reason
  • ☑ Suggest an alternative venue alongside a rejection
  • ☑ Confirm the Coordinator can amend the request to the suggested venue without starting a new search
  • ☑ Confirm the Coordinator is notified of either decision
  • ☑ Record each booking approval, rejection and release with actor, action, affected booking/event and time in the same transaction as the action
  • ☑ Verify all three booking-log outcomes under TC_E06S04_05, TC_E06S04_06 and TC_E06S04_07

Hold a venue tentatively

"Coordinator places tentative holds occupying buffered windows; shipped code follows T-92 (48h default, 1h-14d custom, unlimited logged extensions)."

BDR References: C-01, C-16, C-37, C-60, T-49, C-65, T-66, C-68, T-69, T-78, T-92, O-31, O-32, O-33, O-34, T-102
🔗 Jira Ticket (SCRUM-49) 🔀 Pull Request #245 💻 Source (holds.ts) 🧪 Test (venueHolds.integration.test.ts) 📋 Run Evidence (20261106-081527-Bl0oper-backend-db.md) Coverage: 8 active / 8 total
TC_E06S05_01 TC_E06S05_02 TC_E06S05_03 TC_E06S05_04 TC_E06S05_05 TC_E06S05_06 +2 more
Expand Full Lineage & Technical Proof

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Tentative hold placed

Given a venue is free for the period When I place a tentative hold Then the calendar shows the period as Tentative, the hold is recorded against my event, and the hold carries an expiry date and time set to 48 hours from creation by default, which Venue Staff may change on the hold (assumes O-31)

Scenario 2 — Slot already held or booked

Given a venue already has a tentative hold or a confirmed booking for the period When I attempt to hold it for another event Then the hold is refused and the occupied buffered window is shown as unavailable, without naming the other event (T-102)

Scenario 3 — Hold becomes a booking request

Given I hold a venue tentatively When I submit a booking request for that venue Then the hold becomes a pending booking request for the same period and the expiry no longer applies, because submitting the request is the action that completes the hold; an expired hold cannot be converted (confirmed O-32, T-78)

Scenario 4 — Hold released

Given I hold a venue tentatively and no longer need it When I release the hold Then the period returns to Free on the calendar

Scenario 5 — Hold occupies the buffered window

Given a venue has a setup time of 30 minutes and a turnaround time of 45 minutes When I hold it tentatively for 10:00 to 12:00 Then the hold occupies 09:30 to 12:45, the calendar shows that window as Tentative, and another hold or booking request overlapping any part of it is refused (C-65, T-66)

Scenario 6 — Hold expires and frees the venue

Given my hold's expiry date and time has passed and I have not submitted a booking request for it When the expiry job next runs Then the hold's status becomes Expired, the period returns to Free on the calendar, the venue can be held or requested by any event, and an Expired hold is never counted as a Confirmed or Pending booking anywhere, including the E08-S03 confirmation gate (C-68, T-69)

Scenario 7 — Coordinator told at expiry

Given my hold expires When the expiry job runs Then I receive one in-app notice and one email naming the venue, the event and the expiry time, saying the hold has expired and the venue is free; a later run sends nothing more. There is no reminder before expiry (T-92, replacing the O-33 default)

Scenario 8 — Venue Staff may extend a hold

Given a hold has not yet expired When Venue Staff set a later expiry date and time Then the new expiry applies, and the extension is recorded in the activity log with who made it; an expired hold cannot be extended and must be placed again (T-92)

Scenario 9 — Expiry exactly at the boundary

Given a hold expires at 10:00:00 When the expiry job runs at 09:59:59 Then the hold is still Tentative, and when it runs at 10:00:00 or later Then the hold is Expired

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (10 criteria)

  • ☑ Place a tentative hold on a venue that is free for the period
  • ☑ See the period shown as Tentative on the venue calendar
  • ☑ Be refused when the slot already has a tentative hold or a confirmed booking for another event
  • ☑ Convert a tentative hold into a booking request
  • ☑ Release a tentative hold, returning the period to Free
  • ☑ Confirm only one active hold or confirmed booking exists per venue and period
  • ☑ See the expiry date and time on every hold, defaulting to 48 hours after creation (assumes O-31)
  • ☑ Confirm an expired hold frees the venue and is never treated as a booking
  • ☑ Receive one notice, in-app and by email, when a hold expires (T-92)
  • ☑ Confirm Venue Staff can extend an unexpired hold and the extension is logged (assumes O-34)

"Prevents booking race and double-booking: PostgreSQL exclusion constraint blocks overlapping holds or bookings across buffered occupancy windows (T-100)."

🔗 Jira Ticket (SCRUM-50) 🔀 Pull Request #378 💻 Source (decisions.ts) 🧪 Test (venueClaimPolicy.integration.test.ts) 📋 Run Evidence (20261106-081527-Bl0oper-backend-db.md) Coverage: 8 active / 8 total
TC_E06S06_01 TC_E06S06_02 TC_E06S06_03 TC_E06S06_04 TC_E06S06_05 TC_E06S06_06 +2 more
Expand Full Lineage & Technical Proof

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — First accepted claim reserves the buffered slot

Given a venue has no active overlapping Pending, Confirmed or unexpired Tentative booking When a hold or booking request is successfully accepted Then its current buffered window is claimed for that venue

Scenario 2 — Later overlapping claim refused

Given an active claim reserves a venue's buffered window When another hold or booking request overlaps it Then the new claim is refused, the ordinary Coordinator response identifies the occupied buffered window as unavailable without disclosing another event's title or private booking details, and the active claim remains unchanged

Scenario 3 — Concurrent claims fail safely

Given two new holds or booking requests concurrently claim overlapping buffered windows on one venue When both are processed Then exactly one claim is accepted and the other receives 409 without an extra row or side effects

Scenario 4 — Approval rechecks current buffered availability

Given a request was accepted while its buffered window was available and the venue buffers later change When Venue Staff attempt approval Then current availability, concurrency and buffer values are rechecked; C-109 conflicts stay flagged and retained, and approval is blocked until Venue Staff reject one conflicting Pending request with a reason or an authorized Coordinator withdraws/replans one request. The remaining now-free Pending request may then be approved; a Rejected request is terminal and is never approved. No claim is silently released or selected as a winner. Exactly adjacent half-open buffered windows remain available.

Scenario 5 — Conflicts are per venue, not per event

Given one event has claims on two different venues over the same period When both requests are approved Then both become Confirmed, because conflict detection is per venue and an event may legitimately occupy several venues at once (C-67, T-68)

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (8 criteria)

  • ☑ Confirm the first successfully accepted hold or request claims its venue's buffered slot
  • ☑ Be refused a later overlapping hold or request while the first claim remains active
  • ☑ Confirm concurrent overlapping new claims yield one accepted claim and one 409 with no extra row or side effects
  • ☑ Recheck current availability, concurrency and buffer values at approval
  • ☑ Retain and flag bookings under C-109 after a later buffer change; block approval while the conflict remains
  • ☑ Resolve a conflict explicitly by rejection, withdrawal or replan before a later approval succeeds
  • ☑ Allow exact adjacency of half-open buffered windows and refuse a one-minute overlap
  • ☑ Confirm conflicts are per venue, so one event may confirm overlapping bookings on different venues

🔗 Jira Ticket (SCRUM-260) 🔀 Pull Request #421 💻 Source (bookingPrimary.ts) ⚠️ Run Evidence: Pending Test Cases Coverage: 0 active / 0 total
Expand Full Lineage & Technical Proof

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Venue Staff set the hold expiry

Given a Coordinator requests a tentative hold for a free venue and period When the responsible Venue Staff set an expiry date and time for that hold Then the resulting Tentative hold records that staff-configured expiry and reserves its venue window; no fixed default duration is applied

Scenario 2 — No active hold without a configured expiry

Given no Venue Staff expiry has been set for a requested hold When the request is viewed or another booking is checked Then it is not represented as an active Tentative hold or an indefinite reservation

Scenario 3 — Coordinator chooses the warning time

Given a Tentative hold has a staff-configured expiry When the Coordinator sets a warning time for that hold Then the system records that warning for the hold and notifies the Coordinator before or at expiry according to the configured time

Scenario 4 — Expiry frees the venue

Given a configured hold reaches its expiry without becoming a booking request When the expiry processing runs Then the hold becomes Expired, the venue window is freed, and a Coordinator who still needs it must submit a new request

Scenario 5 — Venue Staff update an unexpired hold

Given a Tentative hold has not expired When Venue Staff update its expiry Then the new expiry applies and the Coordinator is notified of the change; the update does not create a second hold for the same reservation

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (5 criteria)

  • ☑ Set an explicit per-hold expiry as Venue Staff; do not apply a fixed default
  • ☑ Refuse to treat an unconfigured request as an indefinite active hold
  • ☑ Set a per-hold Coordinator warning and notify before or at expiry
  • ☑ Expire an unused hold, free the venue, and require a new request if needed
  • ☑ Update an unexpired hold as Venue Staff and notify the Coordinator

Given a request belongs to one Event When a Session from a different Event is selected Then the request or reservation is rejected and no cross-event link is saved

Given Technical Support Staff are assigned to support an Event When Sessions are added or changed Then the staff assignment remains event-level unless a separate accepted requirement changes it

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (4 criteria)

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Reduced usable stock flags reservations

Given an item has total stock 10, four units withdrawn and five units reserved for the same future period When I reduce total stock to 8 Then the save succeeds, the reservation remains reserved but is marked for review, and its assigned active Coordinator receives one notification and an outbox record

Scenario 2 — Only simultaneous remaining demand counts

Given reservations and dated withdrawals have different or adjacent periods When I reduce total stock Then only simultaneous demand in each reservation's remaining period is compared against the new stock; a withdrawal starting midway through the reservation is included, non-overlapping withdrawal quantities are not summed, and exact fits are not flagged

Scenario 3 — Notification failure rolls back the edit

Given a stock reduction would flag a reservation because of a withdrawal When notification persistence fails Then the stock change, new review flag and notification all roll back

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (5 criteria)

  • ☑ Include dated withdrawals and their start boundaries in catalogue capacity checks
  • ☑ Preserve half-open adjacency and ignore ended demand
  • ☑ Keep reservations intact while flagging shortages
  • ☑ Notify each affected assigned active Coordinator once per stock edit
  • ☑ Roll back stock, flags and notification/outbox writes together on failure

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — All arrangements complete, event submitted for safety review

Given every venue booking on the event is Confirmed or has been withdrawn, at least one is Confirmed, its full requested equipment is reserved and any requested technical support is assigned When I submit the event for its Operational Safety Check Then the status becomes Safety Review, the Safety Officer is notified, the Organiser is told the event is awaiting its safety check, and the event becomes Confirmed only when the Safety Officer approves it (E08-S06) (C-67, T-68, C-70, T-71; assumes O-28, O-39, O-40)

Scenario 2 — Missing venue blocks submission

Given the event has no Confirmed venue booking, or any of its venue bookings is still Pending or Conflicting When I try to submit for safety review Then submission is blocked and each outstanding booking is listed by venue (assumes O-28)

Scenario 3 — Partial equipment blocks submission

Given the event has only a partial equipment reservation When I try to submit for safety review Then submission is blocked and the outstanding quantity is shown

Scenario 4 — None required does not block

Given the event was submitted with 'none required' for equipment When I submit it for safety review Then that requirement counts as fulfilled and does not block submission

Scenario 5 — Outstanding support assignment blocks submission

Given the event requested technical support and no staff are assigned When I try to submit for safety review Then submission is blocked

Scenario 6 — Organiser sees confirmed arrangements

Given an event has been confirmed When the Event Organiser views it Then every confirmed venue with its purpose and period, the date, time and arrangements are shown

Scenario 7 — Confirmed is reached only through approval

Given an event is in Safety Review When anyone other than a Safety Officer attempts to set its status to Confirmed Then the action is refused and recorded in the activity log (C-70, T-71)

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (7 criteria)

  • ☑ Submit an event for its Operational Safety Check once every venue booking is Confirmed or withdrawn, equipment is fully reserved and technical support is assigned, moving it to Safety Review with the Safety Officer notified
  • ☑ Be blocked from submitting while the event has no Confirmed venue booking or any booking still Pending or Conflicting, with each one listed (assumes O-28)
  • ☑ Be blocked from submitting while an equipment reservation is partial, with the shortfall shown
  • ☑ Confirm an event whose equipment requirement was recorded as 'none required'
  • ☑ Be blocked from submitting while a requested technical support assignment is outstanding
  • ☑ Confirm the event becomes Confirmed only through the Safety Officer's approval (E08-S06), never directly
  • ☑ Confirm the Event Organiser is notified with the full confirmed details

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Manual reversion records a reason

Given an event is Confirmed When I deliberately revert it to Planning and record a reason Then the status becomes Planning and the Event Organiser is notified with the reason

Scenario 2 — Registered Attendees notified on deliberate reversion

Given registered Attendees exist When I deliberately revert the event Then they are notified that arrangements are being revised

Scenario 3 — Other broken arrangements remain flagged

Given a non-venue arrangement breaks on a Confirmed event When the owning workflow flags it Then the affected arrangement is flagged and the Coordinator can use the deliberate reversion workflow; venue-block loss follows Scenario 5

Scenario 4 — Arrangements reconfirmed and safety review starts automatically

Given a reverted event has all required venue and technical arrangements confirmed again When the final required arrangement is confirmed Then the event enters Safety Review automatically, the Safety Officer is notified, and the previous safety decision remains in history but is not reused (C-132, T-82)

Scenario 5 — Venue loss automatically returns event to Planning

Given a block makes a Confirmed event's active venue booking unavailable When the block is saved Then the event returns to Planning/change review automatically, the assigned Coordinator is notified immediately, and the event is not cancelled (C-120, T-81)

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (6 criteria)

  • ☑ Deliberately revert a Confirmed event with a recorded reason
  • ☑ Notify the Organiser and registered Attendees on deliberate reversion
  • ☑ Flag other broken arrangements and retain the deliberate reversion action
  • ☑ Automatically enter Safety Review after all required arrangements are reconfirmed
  • ☑ Automatically return a Confirmed event to Planning and notify its Coordinator on venue loss
  • ☑ Retain earlier safety decisions in history without reusing them

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Auto-completed after the end time

Given an event is Confirmed and its end time has passed When the system next evaluates it Then the status becomes Completed

Scenario 2 — Marked complete manually

Given an event is Confirmed and has already started When I mark it complete Then the status becomes Completed

Scenario 3 — Premature completion blocked

Given an event is Confirmed and has not yet started When I try to mark it complete Then the action is blocked

Scenario 4 — Cancelled event never auto-completes

Given an event is Cancelled When its original end time passes Then it is not auto-completed and remains Cancelled

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (5 criteria)

  • ☑ Confirm an event auto-completes once its end time has passed
  • ☑ Mark an event complete manually once it has started
  • ☑ Be blocked from marking an event complete before it has started
  • ☑ Confirm a cancelled event is never auto-completed

Conduct the Operational Safety Check as the Safety Officer

SAY THIS FIRST (10-SEC HOOK)

"Safety Officer assesses event safety factors; approval directly transitions event to Confirmed per T-107 without a second coordinator click."

Known Limitation / Boundary: Rejection or change requests return event to Planning with mandatory comments; coordinator must adjust arrangements and resubmit.
BDR References: C-70, T-71, T-72, T-73, T-74, O-39, O-40, O-41, O-42, O-43
🔗 Jira Ticket (SCRUM-158) 🔀 Pull Request #392 💻 Source (safetyReturn.ts) 🧪 Test (roleQueues.test.ts) 📋 Run Evidence (20261106-081527-Bl0oper-backend-db.md) Coverage: 6 active / 6 total
TC_E08S06_01 TC_E08S06_02 TC_E08S06_03 TC_E08S06_04 TC_E08S06_05 TC_E08S06_06
Expand Full Lineage & Technical Proof

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Events awaiting review listed with what the check needs

Given events are in Safety Review When I open my queue Then each shows the event name, date and time, every confirmed venue with its capacity, layout and known restrictions, expected attendance, accessibility requirements, equipment and its placement, and the time it entered Safety Review, oldest first

Scenario 2 — Structured review of the listed factors

Given I open an event from the queue When I conduct the check Then I record, for each of expected attendance against capacity, venue capacity and layout, emergency access, accessibility requirements, equipment placement, crowd movement and known venue restrictions, whether it is satisfactory, with a comment, before choosing an overall decision (assumes O-42)

Scenario 3 — Approval confirms the event

Given every factor is satisfactory When I approve Then the status becomes Confirmed, the Organiser and the Coordinator are notified with the confirmed details (E08-S03 Scenario 6 and E11-S01's "Event confirmed" row apply), and the activity log records my decision, my identity, the time and the completed checklist

Scenario 4 — Requesting changes returns the event to planning

Given one or more factors are unsatisfactory When I request changes and record which factors and why Then the status becomes Planning, the Coordinator and the Organiser are notified with the items to address, the affected venue or technical arrangements are flagged for re-review, the decision is logged, and the event cannot become Confirmed until it is resubmitted (E08-S03) and approved (assumes O-41)

Scenario 5 — Rejecting the safety arrangement does not cancel the event

Given the safety arrangement as a whole is unacceptable When I reject it and record the reason Then the status becomes Planning with a visible "safety arrangement rejected" flag and the reason, the Coordinator and the Organiser are notified, the event is not cancelled, and the Coordinator may rework and resubmit or cancel it through E10-S04 (assumes O-41)

Scenario 6 — Reason required for reject or request changes

Given I choose reject or request changes When I have not recorded a reason Then the decision is refused until I do

Scenario 7 — Only a Safety Officer decides

Given I am a Coordinator, an Event Coordinator Lead or any other role When I attempt to approve, reject or request changes on an event in Safety Review Then the action is refused and recorded in the activity log

Scenario 8 — Events confirmed before this story are not re-reviewed

Given an event was Confirmed before the Operational Safety Check existed When the check is introduced Then that event keeps its status, has no safety record and is not placed in Safety Review (assumes O-43)

Scenario 9 — Status display and deactivation treat Safety Review as active

Given an event is in Safety Review When its Organiser tracks it (E03-S05) Then "Safety Review" and the date it was reached are shown in plain language; and Given its Coordinator attempts to deactivate their account (E01-S11) Then Safety Review counts as an active-lifecycle status and deactivation is blocked (T-52)

Scenario 10 — Every decision is auditable

Given I approve, request changes or reject When the decision completes Then the activity log holds an entry with my identity, the action (safety check approved, changes requested or rejected), the event, the time and the checklist, immutable as E14-S02 requires

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (8 criteria)

  • ☑ See every event awaiting its safety check with the information the listed factors need, oldest first
  • ☑ Record each factor as satisfactory or not, with a comment, before deciding
  • ☑ Approve an event, making it Confirmed with the Organiser and Coordinator notified
  • ☑ Request changes or reject with a mandatory reason, returning the event to Planning without cancelling it and flagging the affected arrangements
  • ☑ Be refused as any role other than Safety Officer
  • ☑ Confirm events already Confirmed before this story are untouched
  • ☑ Confirm the status tracker shows Safety Review and the deactivation block counts it
  • ☑ Confirm every decision is in the activity log

Given I already have an active registration for an Event When I attempt to submit another registration for that Event Then ConnectSphere tells me I am already registered and does not create a second active registration; selecting multiple Sessions remains part of the existing registration

Scenario 5 — Event and Session venue information shown

  • ☑ Receive one confirmation with Event and selected Session details
  • ☑ Be prevented from creating a second active registration for the same account and Event
  • ☑ Be blocked with missing required information identified
  • ☑ Be refused registration for an Event that is not Confirmed

Enforce registration capacity

SAY THIS FIRST (10-SEC HOOK)

"Enforces both per-session layout capacity and combined attendee capacity; over-capacity submissions route to Pending for Organiser review (T-85)."

Known Limitation / Boundary: Parent event row locked FOR UPDATE during seat decrement to serialize concurrent registrations against race conditions.
BDR References: C-05, C-58, C-78, C-98, T-30, T-31, T-50, T-85, B-11, T-98
🔗 Jira Ticket (SCRUM-64) 🔀 Pull Request #362 💻 Source (capacity.ts) 🧪 Test (attendeeCapacity.integration.test.ts) 📋 Run Evidence (20261106-081527-Bl0oper-backend-db.md) Coverage: 9 active / 11 total
TC_E09S02_01 TC_E09S02_02 TC_E09S02_03 TC_E09S02_04 TC_E09S02_06 TC_E09S02_07 +5 more
Expand Full Lineage & Technical Proof

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Both capacity limits enforced

Given a registration selects one or more Sessions When the request is within each selected Session's approved layout capacity and within the combined Event capacity Then it may be confirmed; if either limit would be exceeded it is not confirmed as an approved seat (C-78, T-85)

Scenario 2 — Over-capacity submission remains Pending

Given an Attendee submits a registration that would exceed a selected Session capacity or the combined Event capacity When it is received Then it is saved as Pending for the Event Organiser to approve or reject and does not count as an approved seat (C-98, T-85)

Scenario 3 — Pending request approval rechecks both limits

Given a registration is Pending When the Event Organiser approves it Then approval succeeds only if both the selected Session capacities and combined Event capacity remain available; otherwise it stays unapproved until capacity/arrangements change or it is rejected

Scenario 4 — Concurrent submissions do not overbook

Given one approved seat remains in a Session or in the combined Event capacity When two registrations are submitted at the same time Then at most one is confirmed against that remaining capacity and any other submission that exceeds capacity is Pending

Scenario 5 — Waiting list remains event-level

Given the combined Event capacity is full When an Attendee opens registration Then the existing Event-level waiting-list option is offered where enabled; a full selected Session follows the Pending decision path and has no separate Session-level waiting list (T-98)

Scenario 6 — Manual addition allowed within both limits

Given normal registration is full but both the selected Session and combined Event capacity have room When the Event Organiser manually adds an Attendee Then the registration is created as a distinguishable manual addition (C-58, T-50)

Scenario 7 — Manual addition blocked at either limit

Given the selected Session or combined Event capacity is already full When the Event Organiser manually adds an Attendee Then the addition is blocked and neither capacity is exceeded

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (7 criteria)

  • ☑ Set combined Event capacity from confirmed Session layout capacities
  • ☑ Enforce both every selected Session capacity and combined Event capacity
  • ☑ Keep an Attendee over-capacity submission Pending for Organiser review without counting it as an approved seat
  • ☑ Recheck both limits when the Organiser approves a Pending registration
  • ☑ Prevent concurrent requests from exceeding either limit
  • ☑ Offer the Event-level waiting list when combined Event capacity is full; keep a full selected Session on the Pending decision path with no Session-level waiting list (T-98)
  • ☑ Allow manual VIP additions only within both limits and block them at either limit

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Joined a full event's list

Given the combined Event capacity is full and its Event-level waiting list is enabled When I join the waiting list Then I am added to the Event-level list and told I will be notified when a place is released; no Session-level waiting list is created (T-98)

Scenario 2 — Released place notified to all

Given a place is released in an event with a waiting list When the place becomes available Then all waitlisted Attendees are notified and the place is claimed on a first-come, first-served basis

Scenario 3 — Claimed place leaves the list

Given I claim a released place When my registration completes Then I am removed from the waiting list

Scenario 4 — Disabled list offers nothing

Given the waiting list is disabled for an event When the event is full Then no waiting list is offered

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (6 criteria)

  • ☑ Join the waiting list for a full event where the list is enabled
  • ☑ See confirmation that I have joined
  • ☑ Receive a notification when a place is released
  • ☑ Claim a released place on a first-come, first-served basis
  • ☑ Leave the waiting list
  • ☑ Confirm no waiting list is offered when the Organiser has disabled it

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Change request recorded

Given my Event has been approved or confirmed When I submit a change request describing what should change Then the assigned Coordinator is notified and the request is recorded against the Event

Scenario 2 — Confirmed details shown alongside

Given a change request is Pending When I view my Event Then the currently confirmed details are shown alongside the pending request

Scenario 3 — Refused edit offers the form

Given I attempt to edit a restricted field directly after approval When the edit is refused Then I am offered the change-request form pre-filled with that field

Scenario 4 — Approved change applied

Given the Coordinator approves my change request When it is applied Then the Event is updated and I am notified

Scenario 5 — Declined request communicated

Given the Coordinator declines my change request When the decision is recorded Then I am notified and the confirmed Event details remain unchanged

Scenario 6 — Terminal Event closes pending requests as Obsolete

Given the Event becomes Completed or Cancelled while one or more change requests are Pending When the Event reaches that terminal status Then each Pending request becomes Obsolete, the transition is recorded in history, and Obsolete is distinct from a Coordinator rejection (C-77, T-88)

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (5 criteria)

  • ☑ Submit a change request against an approved or confirmed Event
  • ☑ See current confirmed details alongside a pending request
  • ☑ Reach the change-request form when a restricted direct edit is refused
  • ☑ Be notified when the Coordinator approves or declines the request
  • ☑ Confirm Pending requests become Obsolete with history when the Event becomes Completed or Cancelled

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Session attendance beyond capacity flagged

Given a Session has a confirmed venue booking When its expected attendance changes Then each booking whose own headcount is set uses that headcount, otherwise it uses the Session attendance; only a booking whose governing headcount exceeds capacity is flagged and Venue Staff are notified

Scenario 2 — Description-only edit flags nothing

Given an Event has confirmed venue and equipment arrangements When only its Event description is edited Then no arrangements are flagged

Scenario 3 — Affected Session arrangements shown first

Given a change affects confirmed arrangements When I save it Then I am shown the affected Session bookings, equipment reservations and staffed Technical Support requests before the change takes effect (T-104)

Scenario 4 — Over-subscription warns only

Given a change would make a Session or combined Event registration capacity lower than approved registrations When the change is saved Then I am warned and shown the over-subscription, and no Attendee is automatically removed or waitlisted

Scenario 5 — Session date/time change flags its arrangements

Given a Session date or time changes When the change takes effect Then that Session's venue booking and equipment reservations, and any staffed Technical Support request overlapping its previous time, are flagged for reconfirmation; an Event-wide date/time change flags all of its Session arrangements and every staffed Technical Support request; a flagged Technical Support request counts as outstanding for readiness until Technical Support Staff reconfirm it at the new time (T-104)

Scenario 6 — Affected staff notified

Given a change flags a venue, equipment or Technical Support staffing arrangement When the affected arrangements are identified Then the assigned Venue Staff and Technical Support Staff are notified

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (7 criteria)

  • ☑ Flag only the Session arrangement whose governing headcount exceeds capacity
  • ☑ Leave arrangements unflagged for description-only edits
  • ☑ Show affected Session bookings/reservations before applying a change
  • ☑ Warn about over-subscription without automatically removing or waitlisting Attendees
  • ☑ Flag the affected Session or all Sessions for date/time changes as appropriate
  • ☑ Flag staffed Technical Support requests on a date/time change and let Technical Support Staff reconfirm them at the new time (T-104)
  • ☑ Notify staff responsible for the affected arrangements

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Event cancelled and Session arrangements released

Given an Event Organiser requests cancellation When I cancel the Event and record a reason Then its status becomes Cancelled, all Session venue bookings and equipment reservations are released, calendars/availability are updated, and affected staff are notified

Scenario 2 — Attendees and waiting list notified

Given Attendees are registered or waitlisted for a cancelled Event When cancellation completes Then all are notified

Scenario 3 — Cancelled Event read-only

Given an Event has been cancelled When any user views it Then it is read-only and shows the cancellation reason and date

Scenario 4 — Organiser cancellation becomes a request

Given an Event Organiser attempts to cancel directly When they submit Then the action is recorded as a cancellation request for the Coordinator to action

Scenario 5 — Pending change requests become Obsolete

Given the Event has Pending change requests When cancellation completes Then each request becomes Obsolete and the transition is recorded in history (C-77, T-88)

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (6 criteria)

  • ☑ Cancel an Event and release every Session booking and equipment reservation
  • ☑ Record a reason for cancellation
  • ☑ Confirm venue and equipment availability is restored
  • ☑ Notify registered and waitlisted Attendees and affected staff
  • ☑ Keep the cancelled Event read-only with its reason and date
  • ☑ Close Pending change requests as Obsolete with history

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Lost venue flags the event

Given my event has a Pending or Confirmed venue booking When Venue Staff mark that venue unavailable over the booking's period (E05-S06) Then I am notified, the booking shows as Conflicting on the event, and the event is flagged as needing alternative arrangements; a Confirmed event returns to Planning without being cancelled, and every other arrangement stays as it was (C-120, T-81)

Scenario 2 — Flagged event offers a replacement search

Given my event is flagged When I open it Then the reason category, the period and the affected booking are shown, the original venue, dates and requirements are preserved, and I can start a venue search (E06-S01) for the same event from that screen

Scenario 3 — Replacement requested without losing the original

Given I have found a replacement venue When I submit a booking request for it (E06-S03) Then the request is created for the same event alongside the Conflicting booking, and I may cancel the Conflicting booking explicitly once the replacement is Confirmed; nothing is cancelled for me

Scenario 4 — Organiser and Attendees told on the actual change

Given my event lost its venue When the replacement booking is confirmed Then the Organiser and registered Attendees are notified of the new venue through the existing venue-change routing (E11-S01), and not earlier (C-121, T-81)

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (5 criteria)

  • ☑ Be notified when a venue I have booked is marked unavailable over my booking, and see a Confirmed event return to Planning without being cancelled
  • ☑ See the reason, period and affected booking on the event, with the original event information intact
  • ☑ Start a venue search for the same event from the flagged event
  • ☑ Request a replacement venue while the Conflicting booking remains on the event until I cancel it
  • ☑ Confirm the Organiser and registered Attendees are told of the venue change only when it actually happens

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Status change notified

Given I am a recipient under the approved routing matrix When an event status changes or a booking decision is made Then I receive a notification stating what changed, when, and which event it concerns, unless I performed the action myself

Scenario 2 — All affected parties notified

Given the event's date, time or venue changes When the change takes effect Then the Event Organiser, assigned Event Coordinator, affected assigned Venue Staff, affected assigned Technical Support Staff, registered Attendees and waitlisted Attendees are notified according to the routing matrix, excluding the acting user

Scenario 3 — Unaffected users not notified

Given a change does not affect a particular user's responsibilities When the change occurs Then that user is not notified

Scenario 4 — Delivered in-app and by email

Given a notification is generated for me When it is delivered Then it appears in the system and is also sent to my registered email address

Scenario 5 — Unread notifications distinguished

Given I have several unread notifications When I open my notification list Then they are shown newest first with unread ones distinguished

Scenario 6 — Marked as read

Given I open an unread notification When I have read it Then it is marked as read

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (11 criteria)

  • ☑ Receive a notification when an event I am linked to changes status
  • ☑ Receive a notification when a booking decision is made
  • ☑ Confirm all affected parties are notified when the event's date, time or venue changes
  • ☑ Confirm unaffected, inactive, withdrawn and unrelated users are not notified
  • ☑ Confirm the acting user is excluded and each recipient gets one notification per logical change
  • ☑ Confirm cancellation preserves recipients before links are released
  • ☑ Confirm internal booking decisions do not reach Attendees
  • ☑ See what changed, when, and which event and event it concerns
  • ☑ Receive the same notification in the system and by email
  • ☑ See notifications newest first with unread ones distinguished
  • ☑ Mark a notification as read
