Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Status change recorded

Given an event status changes When the change completes Then an entry is recorded with the actor, the action, the affected event and the time, and an Event Coordinator permitted to view the event can read it in the event Activity log; access-denial entries are not shown in that log

Scenario 2 — Access denial recorded

Given a user is denied access to an event or screen When the refusal occurs Then an entry is recorded with the user, the target and the time

Scenario 3 — Transferred to E06-S04 Scenario 5 (T-76)

Booking approval, rejection and release logging is accepted under E06-S04. This historical scenario number is retained for traceability and is not an E14-S02 completion criterion.

Scenario 4 — Deactivation recorded

Given an account is deactivated When the action completes Then an entry is recorded

Scenario 5 — Log entries immutable

Given an activity log entry exists When any user attempts to edit or delete it Then the attempt is refused

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (7 criteria)

  • ☑ Record every event status change with actor, action, event and time
  • ☑ Record every denied access attempt with user, target and time
  • ☑ Record every account deactivation
  • ☑ Confirm log entries cannot be edited or deleted by any user
  • ☑ Verify that an Event Coordinator can read the event Activity log within existing event access rules
  • ☑ Confirm access-denial entries, and the names of the users they refer to, are not shown in the event Activity log
  • ☑ Verify denial and deactivation entries in a controlled test database; no Administrator sign-in is required

Expand Full Lineage & Technical Proof

Given-When-Then Acceptance Criteria

Scenario 1 — Both existing readers see Singapore time

Given an authorised Organiser or assigned Coordinator opens the existing event Activity log When an entry displays an edited date/time field value Then each date/time value already displayed by that view uses the existing shared Singapore formatter, including both old and new values where already shown, independently of the browser timezone; 2026-10-15T09:30:00Z represents 15 October 2026 at 17:30 Singapore time, not 16 October. Existing field keys are startAt, endAt and registrationDates; registrationDates stores "opensAt to closesAt", so both endpoints are formatted for display without changing that stored string.

Scenario 2 — Singapore calendar rollover

Given an edited date/time value is 2026-10-15T18:30:00Z When either view displays it Then it represents 16 October 2026 at 02:30 Singapore time; the calendar date as well as the hour is converted correctly.

Scenario 3 — Missing and invalid values keep the existing contract

Given a date/time value is missing or invalid When formatting is needed Then formatDate retains its existing "Not recorded" result; each view retains its existing omission/label-only behavior for absent change values, without throwing, inventing a date or introducing a new fallback.

Scenario 4 — Other values and existing display paths unchanged

Given an entry contains ordinary text, a status change or a venue hold expiry When either view renders it Then ordinary text remains text, existing status labels/badges remain unchanged, and existing hold-expiry formatting and behavior are preserved; the correction is field-aware, not conversion of every date-looking string.

Scenario 5 — Audit evidence and access unchanged

Given the existing event access rules apply When either permitted reader views or reloads the formatted log Then stored UTC old_value/new_value and occurred_at, actor and action remain unchanged and immutable; unauthorised readers remain refused and access-denial entries remain hidden from event logs, with no new audit viewer or permissions.

Definition of Done Verification Checklist (5 criteria)

  • ☑ Scope implementation to the edited date/time value rendering in frontend/src/features/organiser/ClientEvents.tsx and frontend/src/features/events/ActivityLog.tsx using shared formatDate
  • ☑ Cover both views, same-day and rollover boundaries, missing/invalid inputs, other values and immutable/access-preserving reads with TC_E14S03_01 to _06
  • ☑ Do not add before/after history to a view that does not already show it; wider E14-S01 history remains separate
  • ☑ Exclude notification "Changed at ...Z" text, unrelated action/field labels, global viewers, new notifications and changes to stored audit data or hold-expiry behavior
  • ☑ Obtain human code/test review and future T-65/T-93 manual evidence; these planned cases are not execution evidence

⚖️ Team Decisions Register (T-01 to T-108)

107 Canonical Decisions

Full register of engineering architecture and workflow decisions from docs/bdr/B-team-decisions.md. Searchable via ID (e.g. T-79, T-92, T-84) or keyword.

📋 View All 107 Team Decisions (Click to Expand / Instant Search)
T-01 All status-bearing stories

Adopt the fuller Week 4 status list

Rationale: Claris (C-49) named four statuses but said the workflow needs proper discussion later. The Week 4 instructions list draft, submitted, under review, approved, planning, confirmed, completed, cancelled and rejected as examples. The team adopted the fuller list because four statuses cannot express a request returned for clarification, a rejection, or a cancellation, all of which the release must handle. This is a deliberate divergence from something a customer said aloud and is recorded as such.

Follows / Supersedes: C-49
T-02 E08-S03, E09-S01

Bring E08-S03 into release 1

Rationale: E09-S01 requires a Confirmed event, but the whole of E08 sat out of scope, so nothing in the release could set that status. Registration was unreachable.

Follows / Supersedes: C-13, C-39
T-03 E08-S03, E08-S04, E08-S05

Split confirmation into three stories by operation

Rationale: E08-S03 had grown to seven scenarios covering confirm, revert and complete. Applying the OPERATIONS pattern from the story-splitting flowchart produced three stories that each fit a sprint.

Follows / Supersedes: C-48
T-04 E14-S02

SUPERSEDED in part — see T-75 and T-76. Bring E14-S02 in as a reduced-scope enabler

Rationale: E01-S02, E01-S03 and E03-S05 all assert that actions are recorded in the activity history, while the whole audit epic was out of scope. Those criteria could not have passed. Scope limited to status changes, access denials, booking decisions and deactivations.

Follows / Supersedes: Week 1 8f
T-05 E03-S06, E07-S07, E09-S03, E09-S06

Keep four stories that fall outside the twenty core features

T-56 api/events.ts, api/events/index.ts (deleted), backend/tests/eventVisibility.integration.test.ts, .pre-commit-config.yaml, scripts/check_api_routes.py, docs/adr/ADR-014-one-file-per-vercel-serverless-api-route.md, docs/plans/sprint-1-retrospective.md, docs/deploying-and-debugging.md

One file per Vercel serverless API route, function count held at 11

Rationale: Vercel's file-based routing collapses `api/foo.ts` and `api/foo/index.ts` onto the same URL, and the build ships both lambdas without a warning. One silently wins the route; the other is an unreachable slot against the Hobby plan's twelve-function cap. PR #56 (SCRUM-26) added `api/events.ts` next to the pre-existing `api/events/index.ts` from PR #42 (SCRUM-18 hide internal planning info from Attendees, story E01-S03), which made `GET /api/events` return 405 in production for the whole of Sprint 1 and left the organiser browse-events screen backed by ClientEvents.tsx broken without anyone noticing. Adopting one file per URL with method dispatch inside the file eliminates the collision and returns a lambda slot; capping the file count at 11 keeps one slot of headroom so the next story does not land cap-blocked. Enforced by `scripts/check_api_routes.py` as a pre-commit hook and by `.pre-commit-config.yaml`. See ADR-014. Postplan documenting the discovery: <https://4ovp804r75sa.postplan.dev> (v1 misattributed the visibility work to SCRUM-42; correct mapping is SCRUM-18 per `docs/jira-sprint-setup.md`).

Follows / Supersedes: -
T-57 SCRUM-27

A SCRUM-27 draft still requires title, dates and expected attendance

Rationale: SCRUM-27 ("save an incomplete event request as a draft") does not say which of the ten mandatory fields may be left blank. `events.title`, `events.event_range` (the start/end date pair) and `events.expected_attendance` are `NOT NULL` with `CHECK` constraints in `backend/database/migrations/0001_connectsphere_schema.sql`; the other seven mandatory fields are already nullable columns. Making all ten skippable would need a migration relaxing those three constraints, with ripple effects on other modules (`venueBooking`, notifications, audit logs) that may assume every event row has a title, dates and an attendance figure — disproportionate for a 3-point story. Team decision: title, dates and expected attendance stay mandatory for a draft too, validated the same way as a full submission; the other seven skip the missing-field check while `status = 'draft'`. No migration. Confirmed by Aaron on 2026-09-18.

Follows / Supersedes: -
T-58 api/events.ts, backend/src/auth/supabase.ts (deleted), App.tsx, OrganiserRequestFlow, OrganiserDrafts

Cookie sessions everywhere; delete the parallel Supabase Auth wiring

Rationale: Sprint 1 shipped two authentication mechanisms alongside each other: custom cookie sessions (api/auth/session.ts + backend/src/modules/accessControl/sessions.ts) covering login, lockout, verification, and audit-log integration for E01, plus a parallel Supabase Auth bearer-token path in backend/src/auth/supabase.ts that api/events.ts used for organiser create/edit/delete. The two paths did not interoperate. A user who logged in through /api/auth/session had a cookie but no Supabase JWT, so POST /api/events returned 401. App.tsx papered over this by hard-coding `getAccessToken = async () => 'mock-token'`. Team decision: cookie sessions everywhere in Release 1. api/events.ts moves to the same currentUser() lookup the whoami endpoint uses. backend/src/auth/supabase.ts and the server-side @supabase/supabase-js dependency are deleted. Frontend components drop the getAccessToken prop; every fetch uses `credentials: 'same-origin'`. The /prototype route takes an explicit `prototype` prop to opt out of live fetch instead of passing a null access token. See ADR-015. Confirmed by Bryan on 2026-09-17.

Follows / Supersedes: ADR-015
T-59 SCRUM-109, SCRUM-110, backend/tests/*.integration.test.ts, .github/workflows/application-checks.yml

Use a `test` schema in the same Supabase DB instead of a separate test project

Rationale: SCRUM-109 originally provisioned a second Supabase project for `TEST_DATABASE_URL`. That consumes a Supabase free-tier slot on Bryan's account and adds a second DB URL to rotate for every integration test we add. Team decision: create a `test` schema inside the existing sgconnectsphere Supabase project and mirror every `public.<table>` under `test.<table>`. PostgreSQL enforces the schema boundary at the storage layer, so `TRUNCATE test.users` cannot touch `public.users` and no test SQL can accidentally see prod rows. Tests connect with `SET search_path = test, public;`. RLS policies are one-per-schema (small extra config). Rejected alternatives: (a) prod tables with a `test_` row prefix, which leaves TRUNCATE dangerous, (b) prod tables with a JSON `is_test = true` column, which leaves every query at risk of forgetting the filter. Confirmed by Bryan on 2026-09-18.

Follows / Supersedes: ADR-002

Confirmed the team's own precedent already ships the near-identical E05-S02 layout/attendance suitability filter the same way: `searchVenues()` supports a layout/attendance filter in SQL, but `venueApi.ts`/`Venue.tsx` never wire it into any UI, and `tests/e2e/venue.spec.ts` has zero suitability-filter coverage. Team decision (asked via `AskUserQuestion`, confirmed by Aaron before implementation started): ship the accessibility-matching primitive and `searchVenues()`'s `accessibility` param backend-only, covered by unit tests (`backend/tests/venueAccessibility.test.ts`, `venueCatalogue.test.ts`) and an integration test against real Postgres (`venueAccessibility.integration.test.ts`). `TC_E02S03_03` in `tests/e2e/e02.spec.ts` stays `test.fixme`, documented, rather than building a new UI surface for a 1-point story. AC1/AC2 (the organiser-facing predefined checklist and free-text capture) are unaffected and shipped with full UI + e2e coverage, since the organiser request form already exists. Separately, AC1 and AC2 both also say entries are "shown to the assigned Event Coordinator" — there is still no real Coordinator-facing endpoint of any kind (`Coordinator.tsx` reads from `mocks.ts`), the same platform-wide gap already accepted for SCRUM-27's "hidden from Coordinators" AC. Confirmed by teammate "b"'s Jira comments on SCRUM-28, which scope this story as backend-matching-only and never mention Coordinator UI work. Confirmed by Aaron on 2026-09-19.

T-63 E06-S01, E06-S02

T-65 docs/testing/runs/, docs/testing/README.md, AGENTS.md, scripts/check.py (future validator), scripts/export_test_runs_xlsx.py (future exporter), Sprint 1-2 historic backfill

Record a test run in `docs/testing/runs/` whenever the run is used as evidence

Rationale: The team had no execution log: the test-case catalogue in `docs/testing/cases/` says what should be tested, but nothing recorded who ran what, when, against which commit, or with what outcome. The course deliverable needs that ledger in Excel at project end. Decision: one Markdown file per run session under `docs/testing/runs/`, named `YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-<github-username>-<scope>.md`, carrying YAML frontmatter plus a table of TC_ID, test name, outcome and remarks.<br><br>Scope is deliberately narrow. A record is required only when a run is **used as evidence**: cited in a pull request, offered as proof that a story meets its Definition of Done, or shown in a demo. Exploratory runs during development need none, and CI runs are covered by their own immutable Actions log unless someone cites one. An earlier draft said every execution of every test command, which read literally covered every `npm test` while developing and every CI run, and nobody can commit those by hand.<br><br>Session-per-file rather than test-per-file: a file per test result would produce hundreds of files and a conflict whenever two people ran overlapping suites, whereas every session filename is unique by timestamp plus username, so no two people ever edit the same file and merge conflicts are impossible by construction. The `scope` field is a fixed enum so an agent cannot invent values and break the exporter. There is deliberately no BACKFILL outcome: historic runs reconstructed from PR evidence use the normal PASS or FAIL with the correct backdated date and cite their source in the remarks. Records are immutable once merged, so a later catalogue revision never rewrites history.<br><br>This does not replace the per-story traceability matrices (for example `docs/plans/scrum-33-implementation-status.md`), which remain required by the Traceability Standard in `docs/testing/README.md`. Those hold the narrative and the rule-to-test mapping; session records hold the flat exportable execution log. A story log should cite a session filename as well as restating the command, the result, and the exact message seen, so a later report can be matched against what testing saw.<br><br>Raised by Aaron in review of PR #166, who asked that a team-wide obligation be agreed rather than merged on one person's authority. Approved by Bryan on 2026-10-01.

They default to 0 for every existing venue so no data migration changes current availability on its own. A booking's occupancy window is [start minus setup, end plus turnaround]; every availability display and conflict check uses that window instead of the advertised start and end. E05-S03 (calendar) and E06-S01 (search) are Done, so the buffered calendar display and the buffered search are scenarios of E05-S05; E06-S03, E06-S04, E06-S05 and E06-S06 are not started and gain a buffer scenario each in place (T-74). Tentative holds occupy the venue, so they carry the buffers too. Maintenance blocks are a property of the venue itself and are not buffered (O-22). When a buffer is created or changed and an existing booking now overlaps, the booking is flagged as Conflicting and left in place; nothing is released automatically, matching the customer's "identified rather than silently removed". Who sees the flag and whether the save is allowed are O-20 and O-21; the story is written to the defaults recorded there. Add a Safety Review gate between Planning and Confirmed as the interim placement of C-70's Operational Safety Check

Rationale: C-70 says the check happens "after the venue and technical arrangements have been confirmed" and "before the event can proceed to preparation". In the canonical model the moment all arrangements are confirmed is exactly the E08-S03 Confirm gate, and nothing after Confirmed is called preparation. The team's reading is therefore that Confirmed is the state in which preparation may begin, and the safety check sits immediately before it. A new status, Safety Review, is inserted: Planning → Safety Review (the Coordinator submits for review once every arrangement is confirmed) → Confirmed (approved) or Planning (rejected or changes requested, with a mandatory reason and the items to revisit). Neither rejection nor a change request cancels the event. The Safety Officer records a decision against the factors the customer listed; the decision and reason are written to the activity log (E14-S02, ADR-009) and notified to the Coordinator and Organiser through E11-S01. The customer guarantees a response, so no timeout path is built. This placement is interim and is the first question for the Q&A (O-39); if the customer places preparation after Confirmed instead, the status model gains a stage after Confirmed and E08-S05 moves accordingly. Trigger (O-40), reject versus request-changes semantics (O-41), checklist shape (O-42) and retroactive application (O-43) are open and written to their defaults. New stories for the Safety Officer's review screen and the Coordinator's submit-for-review step are added in the backlog PR.

Applied to the Week 7 changes: E03-S01, E05-S01, E05-S03, E06-S01, E03-S05, E01-S01, E01-S02 and E01-S11 are Done and stay Done, with any superseded scenario marked "Superseded by Exx-Sxx (C-nn)" in the backlog rather than deleted and any new behaviour placed in a new story (E06-S01's buffered search in E05-S05; E03-S05's and E01-S11's Safety Review handling in E08-S06); E06-S03, E06-S05, E06-S06, E08-S03, E08-S04, E10-S02 and E11-S01 are not Done and are updated in place; E05-S04 is in the Sprint 2 sprint backlog and is neither edited nor reopened, its correction being the new story under T-67. No Week 7 change is a Scenario 1 or 3 reopening: no original criterion has been found unsatisfied. When a Done story's original criteria could be affected by a new story (E03-S01's status transition, E05-S03's calendar states, E01-S02's Organiser isolation), the new story's test cases include a regression case asserting the original behaviour still holds, per guide step 3.

T-93 `docs/testing/runs/`, manual T-65 records, PR template, AGENTS.md

Keep hand-taken screenshots of manual runs in the repository, named by test case ID

Rationale: Team decision in the team chat on 15 October 2026, agreed by the product owner, after Le Xin asked whether manual runs need screenshots. Practice differed: some testers supplied screenshots in chat, some screenshots came from agent-driven browser runs, and some records were text only. Screenshots kept only in chats or postplans were not durable evidence. Decision: during a manual run (`run_type: manual`) the tester takes the screenshots by hand; agent or Playwright screenshots do not count as manual evidence. Each image is named after the TC_ID it shows and stored with its session record in `docs/testing/runs/evidence/<record filename without .md>/`, and the record links it. Showing the same images in the PR's postplan is recommended best practice, not required; the repository copy is the record. Applies to manual records whose frontmatter `date` is on or after `2026-10-16T00:00:00+08:00`, the day after the decision; earlier records are not retrofitted, because merged records are immutable (T-65), but every Sprint 3 Done story is re-run by its owner with screenshots before the Sprint 3 Review, as a new record; the story stays Done (T-74), and a failing re-run leads to a new user story. A Sprint 3 Done story with no manual record at all (E03-S11) gets its test cases and first manual run, with screenshots, before the review; that is a Definition of Done gap, not a re-run. Sprint 1 and 2 stories are left as they are, because their reviews have happened. The checker does not enforce it yet, so reviewers check the screenshots by hand.

T-96 E06-S03 replacement/withdrawal, E06-S04 suggestions, venue_bookings contract and follow-up migration

Allow replacement retry after withdrawal, but follow the latest rejection's suggestion after rejection

Rationale: Story-owner confirmation on 15 October 2026: a Released replacement no longer prevents a fresh request from the same rejection; retain all historical rows, recheck submission rules and do not reactivate a Released row. A Rejected replacement still consumes its predecessor's suggestion: do not reuse that older rejection to repeatedly request the refused venue. If the replacement's own rejection suggests another venue, the next request references that immediately preceding rejection. There is no fixed two-attempt limit; a rejection without a suggestion ends its suggestion chain. Preserve retry-safe idempotency and one non-Released replacement per rejection. The all-status unique index in merged migration 0019 currently prevents retry after withdrawal; a new coordinated migration must exclude Released replacements only, retaining protection for Rejected and other non-Released rows. Do not edit applied migration 0019 or broaden the index to active-only statuses.

T-104 E10-S02 Scenarios 3, 5 and 6, E10-S02 test cases, E08-S03 readiness, E08-S04 Scenario 4

A date or time change also flags Technical Support staffing for reconfirmation

Rationale: Product Owner answer on 31 October 2026, relayed by the E10-S02 story owner, to a yes/no question raised by the E08-S04 manual run (record 20261031-173321): EVT-1082 moved from 5 to 12 December, its venue booking and equipment reservation were flagged and reconfirmed, but its Technical Support staffing request kept 5 December, counted as Ready, and the event entered Safety Review. Answer: yes. A Session or Event date/time change flags each affected staffed Technical Support request for reconfirmation alongside the venue bookings and equipment reservations, lists it in the change preview and notifies the assigned Technical Support Staff. A flagged request counts as outstanding for readiness, so a previously Confirmed event cannot re-enter Safety Review until it is reconfirmed; reconfirming moves the request and its staff assignments to the new time, refused if an assigned technician is busy then. Adopt PR scope, WIP and reference-source guardrails

Rationale: Team decision on 26 October 2026 after repeated merge conflicts and review churn: new PRs are limited to 40 changed files, 1,800 additions and 1,500 deletions; at most 2 active-policy PRs per human author and 10 active-policy PRs total, with drafts included. T-100 E06-S06 release/product criteria, TC_E06S06_01 to _07, venue-bookings contract

PO interpretation: the first accepted hold or request claims its buffered venue slot; approval rechecks current conditions

Rationale: On 22 October 2026 the Product Owner approved this interpretation of existing customer choices C-01, C-16, C-46, C-60 and C-65; it is not a new customer quote. Pending, Confirmed and unexpired Tentative bookings are active claims, and converting a hold to a request keeps the same claim. The first successfully accepted claim reserves that venue's current buffered window; later overlapping claims are refused while it remains active. Concurrent new claims serialize so one succeeds and a losing request returns 409 without a row or effects. Approval rechecks current availability, concurrency and current buffers. Under C-109, a later buffer edit saves, retains affected bookings and flags the conflict; approval is refused while it remains. Do not silently release a claim, create a FIFO queue or let first approval win. Resolve through explicit rejection, withdrawal or replan before later approval. Keep C-67/T-68: different venues for one event do not conflict, and E06-S03's multiple-venue semantics do not change.

Follows / Supersedes: C-01, C-16, C-46, C-60, C-65; C-67, C-109, T-68

Extend T-37 with XXL=13 for E11-S01

Rationale: Product Owner decision on 1 November 2026 on PR #398: E11-S01 / SCRUM-75 "Notify users about events they are involved in" is thirteen points, not five. T-37's S=1, M=3, L=5, XL=8 has no eleventh or thirteenth step, so 13 is added as XXL, the next value above XL on the team's 1/3/5/8 progression (the Fibonacci continuation 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13). An eleventh point was rejected because it is not a step this team has ever used. The size reflects the story owning the reusable notification capability - recipient routing across status/booking, equipment/support, effective date/time/venue change, cancellation and waiting-list flows; actor, unrelated, inactive and withdrawn filtering; deduplication; private/public content boundaries; transactional inbox/outbox and email outcomes; inbox read state; cross-workflow and database delivery verification - rather than a comparison with E10-S01, which reuses that infrastructure. This is a full-story sizing correction, not thirteen points remaining and not extra sprint credit: the original five-point commitment, the sprint ledger and already-credited work are preserved, and no retroactive velocity uplift is claimed. T-73 continues to govern in-flight work. The estimate alone does not accept the story; E11-S01's Definition of Done, implementation, delivery evidence and PO acceptance stay under SCRUM-75.

C-59 Bryan (G1) Settled

Q: If confirmation requires equipment arrangements to be complete, what about events that need no equipment? Does 'none required' count as complete?

Settled: Confirms T-11's explicit 'none required' option and adds a scenario to E08-S03. Also confirms that the Coordinator and Technical Support Staff decide which requirements are essential.
C-60 Bryan (G1) Settled

Q: Is tentative holding itself in scope for release 1, or only confirmed bookings? 'Not prioritised' is ambiguous between 'no expiry rules' and 'don't build it.'

A: Tentative holding itself is in scope (limited to only one active tentative hold or confirmed booking should exist for a venue/time slot). Specific auto-expiry rules, durations, and placing multiple candidate venues on hold simultaneously are not required/specified for Release 1 and can be proposed by the team if the team feels that it adds value to the organisation.

Settled: Reverses the Week 2 reading. E06-S05 returns to Release 1 (T-49) and the calendar state reverts from Pending to Tentative, amending T-17. The one-hold-per-slot rule confirms T-20. The multiple-candidate-venues part is overtaken by C-67, which allows several bookings per event.**
C-61 Bryan (G1) Settled

Q: If a major change doesn't automatically move an event out of Confirmed, what does the Event Organiser see on a confirmed event whose venue was just blocked?

While the event status remains visible, the system notifies relevant stakeholders of the venue issue so the coordinator can initiate changes. The co-ordinator will contact the Organiser, liaise about the changes offline and reach an agreement with the organiser. Subsequently the co-ordinator will make relevant changes to the event according to the agreement.

Settled: Confirms C-48 and T-28: status never changes automatically. Confirms E05-S04 Scenario 3 and the manual reversion path in E08-S04. Negotiation with the Organiser happens offline.
C-62 Bryan (G1) Settled

Q: Are parallel programme tracks supported? It was mentioned an Event by organiser can have many sessions and different requirements.

Settled: Confirms that E08-S03 blocks confirmation without a ConnectSphere venue. Off-site arrangements are recorded through E03-S06 comments and handled outside the system.
C-64 Yichen (G1) Deferred

Q: How many users is the system expected to support (including attendees)?

A: Exact user capacity numbers (including attendees) are not specified at the moment. The system is expected to support ConnectSphere's growth over the next three years, considering business nature and staff strength (~500 internal staff). Technical teams may propose architecture appropriate for scale.

Settled: Reaffirms C-03. No capacity figure appears in any acceptance criterion. O-17 remains open, and ADR-001 continues to cite the ~500 staff figure as the scale the modular monolith is sized against.
C-65 Customer (W7) Settled

Q: Week 7 Customer Changes, item 1: Venue Setup and Turnaround Time. Customer-initiated change, not an answer to a team question.

A: ConnectSphere has found that simply checking an event's advertised start and end time is not sufficient when determining whether a venue is available. Venue Staff need time before each event to prepare the room and additional time afterwards to reset the venue for its next use. Each venue must therefore have a configurable setup time and turnaround time, and these periods must be included when checking availability and detecting booking conflicts. For example, an event scheduled from 10:00am to 12:00pm with 30 minutes of setup and 45 minutes of turnaround effectively occupies the venue from 9:30am to 12:45pm. Existing bookings that become problematic under the new rule should be identified rather than silently removed.

Settled: **New requirement** (guide step 1): nothing was built for buffers, and the earlier exclusion is withdrawn. Reverses C-18 and C-38. E05-S05 returns to Release 1 (T-66). Setup and turnaround are per-venue attributes maintained through E05-S01; the occupancy window [start minus setup, end plus turnaround] replaces the advertised window wherever availability or conflicts are checked (E05-S03, E06-S01, E06-S03, E06-S04, E06-S05, E06-S06). Bookings that conflict under the new window are flagged, never released automatically. Open: who is shown the flagged bookings (O-20), whether a conflicting buffer change may be saved (O-21), buffers against maintenance blocks (O-22).
C-66 Customer (W7) Settled

Q: Week 7 Customer Changes, item 2: Venue Becomes Unavailable After Booking. Customer-initiated change.

A: ConnectSphere needs Venue Staff to be able to mark a venue temporarily unavailable because of maintenance, equipment failure, renovation, safety concerns, or other operational reasons. This may occur even when future events have already been booked at the venue. When this happens, the existing event itself should not automatically be cancelled. Instead, affected bookings should be identified and the relevant Event Coordinators informed that alternative arrangements are required. The system should preserve the original event information while allowing the coordinator to search for and request a replacement venue.

Settled: **Correction + new requirement**: the correction is to E05-S04 Scenario 2, a team assumption that refused a block over a confirmed booking; the new requirement is the replacement-venue path. Confirms C-48 and C-61 that the event is never cancelled automatically, and goes further: a venue may be made unavailable over confirmed bookings, so E05-S04's refusal of a block over a confirmed booking is withdrawn (T-67). Affected bookings become Conflicting, the Coordinator is notified through E11-S01 and may search for and request a replacement through E06-S01 and E06-S03. E10-S05 returns to Release 1. Open: open-ended unavailability (O-23), status of a Confirmed event that loses its venue (O-24), who else is told (O-25), whether a booking is restored if the venue reopens (O-26).
C-67 Customer (W7) Settled

Q: Week 7 Customer Changes, item 3: Multiple Venues for One Event. Customer-initiated change.

A: ConnectSphere has begun supporting larger events that use several spaces at the same time. For example, a conference may require one auditorium for the main programme and three smaller rooms for breakout sessions. The system must therefore allow a single event to have more than one venue booking. Each venue should be checked independently for suitability, availability, and conflicts, while still remaining associated with the same event. Changes or cancellation of one venue arrangement should not automatically remove the other venue bookings unless this is explicitly required.

Settled: **New requirement** that also corrects a team assumption (T-20, E06-S03 Scenario 3), neither of which the customer had stated. Retires T-20 and inverts E06-S03 Scenario 3: an event may hold several venue bookings, pending or confirmed, at once. Each booking is checked on its own against that venue's availability and conflicts, including the C-65 buffers. Cancelling one booking leaves the others in place unless the Coordinator explicitly cancels them too. E08-S03's "a confirmed venue booking" becomes plural (T-68). The one-hold-per-venue-slot rule from C-60 is unaffected: it is about one venue, not one event. Open: per-booking headcount for suitability (O-27), the confirmation gate across several bookings (O-28), differing time windows (O-29), the venue shown to Attendees (O-30).
C-68 Customer (W7) Settled

Q: Week 7 Customer Changes, item 4: Tentative Venue Holds Expire. Customer-initiated change.

A: Venue Staff have explained that they sometimes temporarily hold a venue while an Event Coordinator is finalising event arrangements. These tentative holds should not reserve a venue indefinitely. Each hold must therefore have an expiry date/time. If the required action is not completed before the deadline, the hold should expire and the venue should become available for other requests. The Event Coordinator should be informed before or when the hold expires, and an expired hold should not be treated as a confirmed booking.

Settled: **New requirement**: expiry was explicitly not required before. Reverses the no-expiry position in C-01, C-16 and C-60 and amends T-49 (T-69). Every tentative hold in E06-S05 carries an expiry date and time; an expired hold frees the venue, is never treated as confirmed, and the Coordinator is told before or at expiry through E11-S01. Open: who sets the expiry and the default (O-31), the action that stops expiry (O-32), reminder timing (O-33), extension (O-34).
C-69 Customer (W7) Settled

Q: Week 7 Customer Changes, item 5: Addition of Event Coordinator Lead Role. Customer-initiated change.

A: ConnectSphere has introduced a new internal role, the Event Coordinator Lead, who is responsible for overseeing incoming event requests and assigning them to individual Event Coordinators. Newly submitted event requests should no longer be assigned directly to an Event Coordinator. Instead, they first enter an unassigned queue that can be viewed by the Event Coordinator Lead. The Lead can review basic event information, assign a suitable Event Coordinator, and reassign events where necessary. Event Coordinators should only be able to manage events assigned to them, while the Event Coordinator Lead should be able to view all coordinator assignments and active events under their supervision. Relevant users should be notified when assignments or reassignments occur.

Settled: **New requirement** (a new role and a new workflow) that supersedes the behaviour of a Done story; E03-S01 stays Done and the queue is a new story (T-74). Adds a sixth role. Supersedes C-41 and C-55: new requests are no longer auto-assigned, so T-14 is retired and new requests go to an unassigned queue the Lead works from (E03-S08, T-70). Coordinators manage only events assigned to them, extending E01-S02 to a second role; the Lead sees every assignment and active event. Assignment and reassignment notify the affected users through E11-S01. Partially supersedes C-56: the Lead may reassign. Accounts are pre-seeded under C-57; ADR-012 one-role-per-account still holds (T-72). Open: one Lead or several (O-35), whether a Lead reassignment needs acceptance (O-36), Coordinator-initiated reassignment requests (O-37), queue visibility (O-38).
C-70 Customer (W7) Settled

Q: Week 7 Customer Changes, item 6: Operational Feasibility Check. Customer-initiated change.

A: ConnectSphere has introduced a new internal role, the Safety Officer, who is responsible for reviewing the operational safety of planned events. After the venue and technical arrangements have been confirmed, the Safety Officer must conduct an Operational Safety Check before the event can proceed to preparation. The review considers factors such as expected attendance, venue capacity and layout, emergency access, accessibility requirements, equipment placement, crowd movement, and any known venue restrictions. The Safety Officer may approve the event, reject the safety arrangement, or request changes. If changes are required, the event returns to the relevant earlier planning stage and affected venue or technical arrangements may need to be reviewed again. The event cannot proceed to preparation until the Safety Officer has approved it. You can assume that the Safety Officer will always give a response (approve/reject/request).

Settled: **New requirement**. Adds a seventh role and a mandatory gate between confirmed arrangements and the event proceeding. "Preparation" is not a status in the canonical model, so T-71 records an interim placement pending O-39. The Safety Officer may approve, reject or request changes; the latter two return the event to the relevant planning stage for re-review, and the event cannot proceed until approved. The customer guarantees a response, so no timeout rule is needed. Decisions are recorded in the activity log (E14-S02, ADR-009) and notified through E11-S01. Open: stage placement (O-39), trigger (O-40), reject versus request changes (O-41), structured checklist (O-42), retroactive application (O-43).
C-71 Dhejassri (G2) Partial

🎯 20-Minute Exam Drill & Defense Runbook

Oral Protocol
Protocol 1: 45-Second Random Story Lookup Drill

When the examiner names an arbitrary story (e.g. "Walk me through SCRUM-47 or E06-S03"):

  1. Type e6s3 or SCRUM-47 into the sticky Proof Router search header.
  2. Recite the SAY THIS FIRST elevator hook word-for-word in 10 seconds.
  3. Click [Expand Full Lineage] to display the exact database migration (0019_venue_bookings_contract.sql) and controller (bookingRequests.ts).
  4. Cite the live test case: "We verify this in backend/tests/venueBookingRequests.test.ts under TC_E06S03_01."
Protocol 2: Handling Concurrency & Race Condition Questions

When the examiner asks "How do you prevent race conditions when two people book the same slot at the exact same millisecond?":

  • State the isolation mechanism: "We use PostgreSQL 17 exclusion constraints with GiST indexes in migration 0016_venue_buffer_write_guard.sql."
  • Quote the lock hierarchy: "For technician staffing, PR #239 prevents 40P01 deadlocks by locking the request FOR UPDATE and the technician user row FOR NO KEY UPDATE."
  • Offer proof: "We prove this with a 25-round real PostgreSQL concurrent race test in backend/tests/staffAssignments.integration.test.ts."
Protocol 3: Gracefully Admitting Known Defects (D-01 to D-04)

If asked about Coordinator Lead queue or copying an event:

  • Never bluff or claim it works: "That is tracked as formal open defect D-01 (SCRUM-256) in docs/testing/defects.md."
  • Explain the root cause cleanly: "The Lead queue and reassignment routes were developed on feature/SCRUM-153 but were unmerged before sprint freeze to protect stability."
  • Demonstrate professional maturity: "Rather than claiming false Done, we committed expected-failure tests (test.fail) so the suite stays green while the defect remains transparently visible."
Protocol 4: Offline Readiness & Emergency Fallback

In the event of room Wi-Fi failure during the assessment:

  • This Postplan Web App is 100% self-contained with zero external CSS, fonts, CDNs, or network scripts.
  • Simply open artifacts/final-qna-prep-guide.html directly in Chrome or Edge locally; instant local search for this static guide functions completely offline.
  • All test cases, scenarios, and architecture proofs remain fully accessible offline. Note that outbound GitHub and Jira links require internet connectivity and appropriate SSO authentication.
Protocol 5: Defending Scrum Velocity & Delivery Accountability

When asked "Why does your velocity vary across sprints, and why does Jira differ from your audit?":

  • State the honest metric: "Raw Jira charts were distorted by unestimated subtasks and technical enablers. We conducted an independent product-story title audit (T-96) to establish true velocity across Sprints 1 to 4."
  • Emphasize DoD governance: "Per team decision T-73, in-flight sprint commitments are not retroactively inflated. We only count user stories verified against the strict Definition of Done."
  • Cite the proof: "Figure 2.3 in Section 01 reconciles Jira chart velocity, fair story audit velocity, and strict DoD verified velocity."
Protocol 6: Defending AI Governance & Test Accountability

When asked "How do you ensure AI-generated code and tests are trustworthy and not fabricated?":

  • Quote the golden rule: "Per instructor guidance and team decision T-65, every test run is captured in immutable execution records under docs/testing/runs/ with git commit and runner attribution."
  • Human manual evidence only: "Per decision T-93, all screenshots must be hand-taken by human testers in step order; AI-fabricated screenshots are strictly prohibited."
  • Zero rubber-stamping: "All AI-generated code and unit tests must achieve 100% code coverage on modified lines and undergo manual peer review before pull request approval."
